statement: Vercel July 2026 shows Jevons absorption: token volume growth exceeded the exact break-even needed to offset realized price deflation.
caveat: Vercel gateway traffic is not the global market

statement: Token-layer monetization is deflating while physical H100 rental pricing is much less deflationary.
caveat: Indices have different perimeters and are snapshots

statement: Open-weight models capture most observed Vercel token volume while proprietary frontier providers retain disproportionate spend.
caveat: Vercel gateway mix is not the global market

statement: Blackwell-era compute content converges near USD 25B per IT-load GW across heterogeneous project estimates.
caveat: Nscale is Rubin-era, greenfield, and islanded; project perimeters differ

statement: Operator revenue per GW must rise materially with Rubin to avoid worsening gross-revenue replacement economics as vendor content per GW rises about 60% from Blackwell.
caveat: Gross revenue payback omits opex, financing, margins, and actual Rubin utilization

statement: Stored evidence does not confirm a current physical compute glut, though forward excess-capacity risk is elevated.
caveat: Requires broader rental, utilization, availability, and contract datasets

statement: SpaceX management guidance is a potential counterexample to generalizing merchant or Nscale monetization to every compute operator. A higher nominal rate could improve replacement economics if its power boundary and persistence are demonstrated.
caveat: No reported PUE or normalized effective-IT denominator established. Group ARR is not compute-only revenue. This does not establish a market-wide Jevons result or validate orbital-compute economics.

statement: OCI demand growth does not establish capital-light economics; customer financing improves funding timing while leases and replacements remain.
caveat: Cash-flow figures are consolidated; no OCI-specific return on capital or margin derived.

statement: CoreWeave's take-or-pay backlog and customer prepayments support funding visibility but do not make the business asset-light: cash capex, debt principal and lease commitments are each material relative to current recognized revenue.
caveat: RPO and deferred revenue are contract measures, not present revenue; total debt includes recourse and nonrecourse structures and lease commitments are undiscounted.

statement: CoreWeave's Q2 all-cloud revenue supports an approximately USD8.24 million per modeled average active-power MW-year reference, but compute-only revenue per effective IT MW is not identified.
caveat: Active-power boundary, service mix, site activation timing, portfolio PUE and physical utilization are undisclosed; the 1.25GW denominator is a linear-ramp proxy, not reported average IT MW.

statement: Nebius's stronger forward contract pricing supports higher monetization potential but does not establish realized revenue per effective IT MW.
caveat: 2027 realization and unknown power perimeter; Q2 raw segment revenue and December exit capacity cannot normalize it.

statement: Customer funding supports expansion but fixed leases, power and accreting debt preserve financing and replacement exposure.
caveat: No company-wide return on capital inferred; prepayments fund timing rather than eliminating lifetime obligations.

statement: IREN's customer prepayments and deferred lease balances improve construction funding timing but do not establish current AI compute revenue.
caveat: Future recognition depends on acceptance, commencement, service delivery and contract terms.

statement: IREN's disclosed forward contract pricing has moved above the older Microsoft contract value per stated IT MW, but the higher markers do not establish realized revenue per effective utilized IT MW.
caveat: Greater-than-$20M is a company claim for recent three-year contracts and approximately $25M refers to discussions; power boundary, active cohorts and utilization remain unmatched.

statement: IREN can ring-fence much of the Microsoft GPU financing in a collateralized SPV, but parent guarantees, large commitments and the FY2027 capex plan preserve financing and replacement exposure.
caveat: Project debt has limited general recourse but specific parent guarantees; customer funding mitigates timing rather than eliminating lifetime hardware and site obligations.

statement: Microsoft's September segment exhibit resolves exact FY2026 Azure revenue but not the AI-compute numerator required for revenue per effective MW.
caveat: Azure includes cloud and AI consumption plus virtual desktop; the FY27 reporting perimeter differs from the earlier Azure-and-other-cloud-services metric.

statement: No defensible Azure AI revenue per effective utilized IT MW range can be calculated from current disclosures.
caveat: The 1 GW Q4 addition lacks a power boundary and time weighting; the 1.55 GW historical implied IT load covers only a narrow FY2025 owned-fleet boundary.

statement: Microsoft's AI and cloud expansion carries a very large fixed and quasi-fixed obligation stack even before replacement economics are modeled.
caveat: Amounts are consolidated and not fully attributable to Azure AI; RPO and OpenAI commitments mitigate demand risk but are not cash received, physical utilization or matched project return.

statement: Microsoft's FY2027 useful-life change will move more datacenter leases from finance to operating classification, reducing reported capex comparability without reducing the underlying investment plan.
caveat: Future classification and the approximately $175B calendar-2026 capex expectation are management guidance; operating lease cash remains an economic commitment even when excluded from capex.

statement: Microsoft's efficiency and token-adoption disclosures are directionally consistent with rapid demand absorption but do not support an exact Jevons break-even.
caveat: No matched realized price, task or token volume and customer-spend series; performance-per-watt and performance-per-dollar claims are hardware/workload claims rather than fleet economics.

statement: AWS capacity delivery and customer funding are linked; contracted demand does not establish capital-light or independently financed demand.
caveat: RPO supports demand visibility; exact compute fees, capacity and cash margins remain unknown. No assertion of improper accounting.

statement: No defensible Google Cloud AI revenue per effective utilized IT MW can be calculated from current disclosures.
caveat: Exact segment revenue and fleet PUE do not supply external AI attribution, active IT MW, utilization or matched architecture mix. Growth excluding TPU sales is real but unquantified.

statement: Google Cloud demand visibility and external-capital structures coexist with a very large consolidated obligation and financing stack; the AI build is not capital-light.
caveat: Commitments, guarantees, financing and backlog are consolidated or have different perimeters; they cannot be netted or assigned wholly to GCP AI. Blackstone equity and RPO mitigate funding/demand risk but are not Google revenue or realized returns.

statement: Public Ironwood chip-hour pricing establishes a billable numerator but not a TPU revenue-per-IT-MW baseline.
caveat: Full-system IT power per chip, realized discounts, paid occupancy and physical utilization are missing. Chip TDP or peak FLOPS cannot substitute for matching system power.
